evidence: src/domain/order-repository.ts and src/domain/product-repository.ts declare only the interfaces OrderRepository and ProductRepository. No module file accesses persistence directly.
src/domain/order.ts: Order.advanceTo and Order.cancel call nextState and isCancellable from src/domain/order-state.ts and do not repeat the transition rules.
src/domain/product.ts: canReserve(quantity) is the single definition of the reservation rule, and reserve() calls it.

src/domain/stock-reservation.ts: reserveStock calls product.canReserve(quantity) and then product.reserve(quantity). It reuses the rule, though it rebuilds the same 'insufficient_stock' error message as Product.reserve.
src/domain/order-line.ts checks for a positive-integer quantity; src/domain/product.ts checks for non-negative on-hand stock. These are separate invariants, each in one place.
src/domain/domain-error.ts: every file reports errors through the single DomainError type and its DomainErrorCode values.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module covers one domain concern: ordering and stock. It has entities (Order, OrderLine, Product), an order state machine (order-state.ts), a domain service (stock-reservation.ts), a shared error type (DomainError) and two repository ports (OrderRepository, ProductRepository). The repository files hold interfaces only; no file uses a database, ORM or query client. Each invariant has one definition. The positive-integer quantity rule is only in the OrderLine constructor. The non-negative stock rule is only in the Product constructor, and it is a different invariant. The transition rules live in order-state.ts (nextState, isCancellable), and Order calls them rather than copying them. The reservation rule lives in Product.canReserve, which both Product.reserve and stock-reservation.reserveStock call. reserveStock does build the same 'insufficient_stock' DomainError with the same message template as Product.reserve. That repeats how the error is reported, but the check itself is a call to one shared definition, and the separate check is needed for the all-or-nothing pre-check. So I count it as a minor smell, not a duplicated rule. Every file uses DomainError and the module's own types consistently, and none bypasses the module's abstractions.
